messages:
Kevin: quick question — we're designing envelope encryption for a new service that spans two subscriptions in the same tenant. do we recommend user-assigned managed identity + RBAC on the Key Vault key, or still use access policies on the vault? worried about least-privilege for unwrap operations and cross-subscription onboarding.
Sara: my strong preference is user-assigned MI + RBAC roles for keys. access policies are legacy and get messy when you need to scope across many principals. RBAC gives role assignments at vault/key level and works better for automation.
Ben: agree with Sara. also call out managed HSM vs standard vault: Managed HSM only supports RBAC and has FIPS/HSM-backed keys, which is nice if you need dedicated KMIP-like guarantees.
Jess: one gotcha — if you need to let external tenants (guest principals) perform unwraps, RBAC + guest invite works but you have to watch tenant boundaries. cross-tenant service principal auth sometimes fails w/conditional access. test end-to-end.
Kevin: thanks. any practical advice for minimizing unwrap counts and cost? unwraps will be hot during batch replays.
Sara: store the DEK (data encryption key) locally in an encrypted cache and only call Key Vault to unwrap when the DEK is expired or rotated. i.e. KEK in AKV wraps DEK. use token caching + short-lived DEK TTLs.
Ben: also enable prefix/KV cache in the service runtime so repeated token streams reuse the same DEK. audit-wise, you’ll see fewer unwrap ops which is easier to monitor.
Kevin: audit/logging — what to enable so security/compliance can prove unwraps and key usage? retention requirements likely 2+ years.
Jess: enable diagnostic settings: send KeyVaultAuditEvents to Log Analytics and export to an Event Hub + storage account for long-term archival. Security wants both the operation and principal (+ caller ip if available).
Ben: example CLI to wire diagnostics quickly:
```bash
az monitor diagnostic-settings create --name akv-diags --resource /subscriptions/<sub>/resourceGroups/<rg>/providers/Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/<vault> --workspace /subscriptions/<sub>/resourceGroups/<rg>/providers/Microsoft.OperationalInsights/workspaces/<la_ws> --logs '[{"category":"AuditEvent","enabled":true}]' --metrics '[]'
```
Kevin: nice. role names? which RBAC role covers wrap/unwrap crypto ops?
Sara: Azure has built-in roles: "Key Vault Crypto User" gives unwrap/wrap/sign/verify for keys. "Key Vault Crypto Officer" is for management. grant the minimal role at the key (not vault) if you can.
Jess: prefer assigning at the key scope: `/subscriptions/.../resourceGroups/.../providers/Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/<vault>/keys/<keyName>` so other keys in the vault aren't exposed.
AKV-bot: deploy event: created key `prod-kek-2026-03` in vault `prod-akv` by `infra-ci` (automated).
Ben: for rotation, automate KEK rotation with a canary period: create new key version, update service to accept multiple key versions for unwrap, rewrap existing DEKs in background, then switch default. keep audit records of rewrap ops.
Kevin: any concerns around key rewrap order or race conditions? we have many shards doing rewrap concurrently.
Sara: implement a leader-driven rewrap job or use a durable queue with idempotency tokens. record rewrap job id in metadata on the DEK record. if job fails retry with backoff.
Jess: also put a short fallback: if unwrap with primary version fails, try previous version(s) for a short window. this handles lag during rollout.
Kevin: last — tenant boundary: what if we need to move a workload to a different tenant/subscription? best practice for key material?
Ben: recommended: never transfer KEKs across tenants. create new KEK in target tenant, then rewrap DEKs using source KEK unwrap + target KEK wrap during a controlled migration window. log every step.
Sara: and revoke old key versions only after verification and a retention window required by compliance. keep archived audit logs.
Kevin: perfect — i'll draft a short runbook from this and circle back for a dry-run. thanks team :thumbsup:
